fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter from get_impress_multi_title_color__82b6d89a to get_impress_multi_title_color__14718ed4f8dc81749072a781b972112d — invalid 8-char suffix replaced with correct 32-char MD5 hash
Fix 2: Renamed metric from check_impress_multi_title_color__82b6d89a to check_impress_multi_title_color__14718ed4f8dc81749072a781b972112d — same correction
Fix 3: Updated evaluator.func and evaluator.result.type in task JSON to match new function names

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly retrieves the saved PPTX file (postconfig saves with ctrl+s) and identifies the topmost text shape as the title for each requested slide.
Slide indices [1, 2] (0-based) correctly map to slides 2 and 3 (1-based) as specified in the instruction.
Expected color '000000' correctly represents black as required by the instruction.
Metric correctly accesses expected dict directly (e.g., expected.get('expected_color_hex', ...)) without wrapping in 'rules' key, which is correct for type='rule' evaluation.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 per slide, 2 slides total) provides appropriate granular scoring and matches the stated task rationale.
All run colors in the title shape are checked, ensuring the entire title text is black, not just part of it.

Minor concern: runs with inherited/theme color (font.color.type is None) produce None in all_colors; the metric check 'all(c is not None and ...)' would fail for those runs even if they visually display as black. In practice, explicitly setting black in LibreOffice sets explicit RGB, so this is unlikely to cause false negatives under normal usage.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: In the getter, when font.color.type is None (inherited color), consider resolving the effective color from the theme or treating it as passing if the effective display color is black, to handle edge cases where partial runs inherit black without an explicit override.
